subject: Region pinning and cross-region failover questions — ZenWell Pharma
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@zenwellpharma.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T14:03:00Z
Subject: Initial questions on data residency & failover (ZenWell)

Diego,

Thanks for the call earlier — quick follow-up from the ZenWell infrastructure team. We have a few compliance-driven asks that determine whether we can move forward with a pilot: PII handling, region pinning, and how cross-region failover/backups are managed. High level: we need to ensure any PII from EU patients stays in EU by default, but we also require an approved cross-region failover plan if US-hosted services are required for DR.

Can you confirm the following items or point me to the right docs/contacts?
- Can we pin production traffic to EU (single region) and keep backups in-region?
- How does Redwood handle automatic failover between regions? Is data replicated cross-region continuously or only snapshots?
- What logging/audit controls do you offer for access to KV caches and request logs (retention windows)?
- Do you support contractual data residency and encryption key control (customer-managed keys)?

I've attached our internal requirements spreadsheet so you can respond inline. Also cc'ing Samir (procurement).

Thanks,
Elena Morales
VP, IT & Compliance
ZenWell Pharma
[Attachment: ZenWell_ResReqs_20261101.xlsx (xlsx, 84KB)]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@zenwellpharma.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T15:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial questions on data residency & failover (ZenWell)

Elena — thanks for the clear list and for the spreadsheet. Quick recap of what we covered on the call and my clarifying questions below. I want to be explicit about recommended configurations and any constraints so your security and procurement teams can evaluate.

Recap / answers at a high level:
- Region pinning: Yes, you can pin inference traffic to an EU region for production (we support per-route region pinning). That keeps live requests routed to EU hosts.
- Backups: Backups (model artifacts + KV cache snapshots) can be configured to remain in-region. By default we provide daily snapshots; cross-region replication is optional and must be explicitly enabled.
- Cross-region failover: Our standard failover mode is an active-primary with passive-secondary. When failover is enabled, data is asynchronously replicated to the secondary region unless you opt into synchronous replication for critical state (note: synchronous replication impacts latency and cost).
- Logs & auditing: We support token-level request logs with configurable retention (30/90/365 days). Audit logs for control-plane actions (model deploys, region changes, key rotations) are retained for 365 days by default and can be exported to your SIEM.
- Customer-managed keys: Yes — we support KMS/HSM integrations. Keys can be customer-managed; we can provide control-plane flows for key rotation and key-handover proofs.

Clarifying questions that will change the recommendation:
1) When you say "keep backups in-region", do you require zero cross-region transfer even for encrypted snapshot replication (i.e., no cross-region replication allowed)?
2) For failover SLA, what RPO/RTO do you need for the pilot (we have standard tiers; e.g., RTO < 5m with synchronous replication vs RTO ~ 10–30m with async)?
3) Do you plan to use Redwood Dedicated/Private (where data plane is entirely in your VPC) or Hosted API for the pilot? Dedicated/Private gives stronger contractual assurances for residency.

Next steps: I can assemble a short residency matrix (region pinning modes, replication options, trade-offs) and loop in Solutions Engineering for a deep-dive. Proposed time: Tue 2026-11-03 09:00–09:30 PT for a technical follow-up. Will that work?

Attached: Redwood-residency-matrix (draft) — includes policy options and default behaviors.

—
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-residency-matrix.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@zenwellpharma.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Kapadia <samir@zenwellpharma.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial questions on data residency & failover (ZenWell)

Thanks Diego — that all aligns with what I expected. A couple of clarifications inline in the attached spreadsheet and answers to your questions:

1) Backups: For Phase 1 of the pilot we require backups to remain in-region (no cross-region replication at rest). For Phase 2 (large-scale) we may permit encrypted cross-region replication if we get contractual assurances and SSE+CMK controls.
2) RPO/RTO: For pilot we can accept RTO up to 15 minutes and RPO up to 1 hour. If you support an async model with warm standby we can meet that.
3) Deployment mode: We prefer Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private (VPC) for the pilot — procurement will not approve a hosted multi-tenant plan for any production traffic.

Also, can Solutions Engineering include a short architecture slide that shows where KV caches and ephemeral inference state live relative to customer data? That will help our InfoSec team.

Samir from procurement is on copy and will coordinate contracting questions.

Best,
Elena
[Attachment: ZenWell_ResReqs_20261101.xlsx (updated)]

Hi team — looping in Monica (Solutions Engineering) to prep the architecture slide and implementation notes. Quick notes from a controls/contract perspective:

- Dedicated/Private: recommended for ZenWell given procurement constraint. We'll document residency guarantees in the SOW and add a clause for backup locality for Phase 1.
- Replication model: we can offer async replication to a passive stand-by in another EU AZ only (no cross-continental replication) for the pilot to satisfy DR testing; cross-continent will be gated and require a dataplane-design review.
- KV caches: ephemeral by default and TTL-configurable; persistent cache snapshots are included in the backup policy. We'll provide an explanatory diagram for where caches live (data plane inside your VPC or our EU host depending on deployment).
- Audit & logs: we can export to your SIEM over TLS and provide a signed export for procurement.

- Monica: create architecture slide + residency matrix (by Tue 2026-11-03 EOD).
